keyVerseText: So he measured the house, an hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, with the walls thereof, an hundred cubits long;
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun בִּנְיָה (binyâh) is derived as a feminine form from the root בָּנָה (bânâh), which means 'to build' in both literal and figurative senses. This root encompasses the acts of constructing, establishing, and continuing, whether it be a physical structure or the establishment of a family. The feminine noun form בִּנְיָה thus emphasizes the result or product of building—a structure or building itself—highlighting the tangible outcome of the creative and sustaining work implied in the root.
usageInScripture: The word בִּנְיָה occurs only once in Scripture according to the data, appearing in Ezekiel 41:13. In this context, it is translated as 'the building,' referring specifically to a part of the temple complex. The consistent translation as 'building' or 'structure' reveals that this term is used concretely to denote a physical edifice, underscoring its role as a measurable and defined construction within the sacred architecture described.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding בִּנְיָה as a building rooted in the concept of building (בָּנָה) invites reflection on God as the ultimate builder and establisher. Just as a physical structure requires careful design, measurement, and stability, so too does the spiritual house—God’s people—require His divine construction and sustaining power. This word reminds believers that God’s work in creation and redemption is purposeful and enduring, calling the church to be a spiritual house built on Christ. The tangible reality of a building points to the visible and lasting nature of God’s kingdom, which He establishes and maintains.
keyVerseReflection: Ezekiel 41:13 records a precise measurement of 'the house' and 'the building' along with its walls, emphasizing the ordered and deliberate nature of the temple's construction. The use of בִּנְיָה here highlights not just any building, but a significant and integral structure within the house of God, reinforcing the theme of divine order and holiness. This word draws attention to the tangible reality of God's dwelling place among His people, inviting believers to appreciate the care and intentionality behind God's presence with His covenant community.
